newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit in range as baht holds steady.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit in range as baht holds steady.

text.p: The ringgit was mildly easier in a narrow range as the baht held steady against the U.S. dollar, dealers said on Friday.
They said the ringgit, which gained nearly 100 points on Thursday on the back of fund outflows from the Thai baht, was still a favoured currency by many fund managers.
However, activity was thin as the market continued to focus on the Thai baht.
"There should be more action in dollar/ringgit after Chinese New Year and Hari Raya (Eid al-Fitr) festivals. The ringgit should make fresh gains," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said if the situation in Thailand did not improve, more funds will flow into other regional currencies.
"Market is worried about Thai baht. There are capital flights from Thai baht to ringgit, but most of it is short-term flows," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
He said ringgit's gains would be limited by fresh dollar buying around 2.4820, despite flows from the baht and Japanese funds looking to put funds in Malaysia.
"The market will be thin because it is the last day of the month. This will restrict movements," a Malaysian dealer said.
At 0300 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.4860/70 a dollar.
